surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: The Flames get their first win at last
paras: The Flames won for the first time this season, at the sixth try, after starting 0-5-0. The Ducks’ Roger McQueen played his first NHL game. Adam Klapka struck first for the Flames midway through the first. Beckett Sennecke and Leo Carlsson scored just under two minutes apart later in the period to turn a 1-0 deficit into a 2-1 lead, and that was all they would get. Midway through the second, Aydar Suniev tied it 2-2 for Calgary, and Jeff Malott and Klapka squared off. Martin Pospíšil put the Flames ahead for good with less than five minutes left. Yegor Sharangovich added the empty-netter with less than two minutes left to make it 4-2.

The Flames had a bit more of the good stuff, outshooting the Ducks 36-25. Wolf shook off a shaky start for the Flames, allowing two goals on the first seven shots and none on the last 18, and Lukáš Dostál stopped 32 of 35 at the other end.

The Ducks killed off a two-man advantage that lasted two minutes early in the second. The Flames improved to 1-5-0, still last in the NHL, while the Ducks dropped to 4-2-0, slipping to fourth in the Pacific.
